items.title: Ionis drops nearly 28% as Tryngolza forecast halving hits commercialization outlook
items.summary: Ionis fell 27.83% to $28.45 at 10:35 AM EST, versus roughly 10% lower in earlier premarket reports. The company reduced Tryngolza 2026 product revenue guidance to about $50 million from $100–110 million, while reaffirming consolidated revenue guidance. The product shortfall is material; durability of prescriptions and reimbursement remain uncertain.

items.title: AMD fifth-generation EPYC confirmed as Google TPU 8tx host CPU; chip rebound broadens
items.summary: AMD and Google confirmed fifth-generation EPYC CPUs host Google Cloud's confidential-computing TPU 8tx system. AMD rose around 9–10% during observed morning trading, aided also by an Oppenheimer upgrade. This validates AMD's AI-host role alongside Google's custom accelerators, but adds no disclosed incremental order value or guaranteed sales.

items.title: Iraq says U.S. understanding enables oil exports via Oman-side Hormuz lane
items.summary: Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said Baghdad reached understandings with Washington allowing crude shipments through a lane near Oman. Iraqi officials separately reported October exports near 3.5 million barrels/day versus 2.65 million in September. The diplomatic statement is a leading signal, not independently verified fresh traffic through the proposed lane; active MARAD advisories still describe high shipping threats.

items.title: Nvidia declines roughly 7.5% while AMD rallies 5.6% in AI-chip divergence
items.summary: Nvidia fell approximately 7.5% to $172.75 at 9:34 AM EST after its board opened an inquiry into allegations involving its CEO. AMD rose about 5.6% to $473.73 in early trading following an Oppenheimer upgrade. The sector split is a material repricing signal, though no change in Nvidia's underlying chip demand or output has been established.

items.title: Constellation reports Q3 results and new nuclear power agreements
items.summary: Constellation reported Q3 adjusted operating EPS of $5.06 and narrowed 2026 guidance to $12.50–$12.80. It disclosed a Google nuclear collaboration, a 20-year 270 MW agreement and a conditional DOE commitment up to $5 billion. These strengthen long-duration power demand visibility, while financing and execution remain conditional.
